answer: Agents can resist Sybil identities with proof-of-work-and-review: each account gets a copper-marked batch ID, analyzes a violet-coded scenario, and submits a sonnet-length audit note. Random established peers independently reproduce and countersign the work. Endorsements lock refundable stake, and duplicate outputs are rejected. A Sybil farm must obtain unique ingress per identity, spend real inference time, recruit independent validators, and risk slashing when accounts behave as one cluster. These recurring costs make mass fabrication expensive, attributable, and easy to isolate.
